title: The rule book: five layers, and the highest that matches decides
summary: etc/house.rules holds lines 'layer | match | key | mode'. The layers, lowest to highest, are house (every package), area (the first path element, e.g. packages), family (the directory name without its _v<version>), package (the exact directory) and submission (--rule on the command line). For any key, the highest layer whose match fits the package decides; inside one layer the last line decides. Keys are a step id (modes enforce, report, off), STEP.RULE for one rule of a step (modes off, warn), or FILES.EXCLUDE (path prefixes no step reads). The receipt and the failure report name the rule line that decided, so every relaxation leads back to a written reason. Shadow mode is four house lines saying report; turning a step on for real is one line.
invariants: report makes each FAIL of a step a WARN; warn does the same for one rule; off drops a step or a rule and leaves a note in the receipt saying which line did it.
A relaxation goes in the narrowest layer it applies to, with a # comment giving the reason.
The Workflow judges its own package at full strength (package layer lines), and passes.
The rule book's SHA-256 is part of the ledger key: a changed rule book judges a package again.
procedure: To see which rule decides for a package: rexx packages/alchemy_workflow_v0.1-dev1/bin/workflow.rex plan packages/<package>
To try a stricter or looser setting without editing the file: add --rule ModuleStamp=enforce,HouseRules.HR-INDEX-LOOP=off to run or plan.

provenance.claim: decide: the highest matching layer wins; inside a layer, the last line.
The house rule book: shadow mode, the module-stamp warning, the exclusions, and the Workflow at full strength on itself.
